subject: Re: Proposal: split Premium Support SKUs + explicit escalation path
messages:
From: Maria Olson <maria.olson@olsondata.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@olsondata.com>, Olson Data Procurement <procurement@olsondata.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Support packaging questions

Thanks for the deck, Karthik — quick follow-ups from our side as we evaluate the Dedicated + support add-on: 

1) We need clearer separation between uptime crediting (per-downtime SLA) and response SLA (first touch / incident routing). Can you confirm whether credits are pro-rated by incident length or calendar minutes?
2) For the proposed 1-hour P0 response, does that include acknowledgement or full mitigation? Our SREs expect an on-call engineer assigned within an hour.
3) We have procurement constraints: list price + approved discount bands. Can you provide an explicit discount table for 12/24 month commits and whether the support retainer can be structured as a per-seat seat-based retainer vs per-incident credits?

Also, Tom raised a question about escalation coverage across APAC midnight hours — he wanted to see an escalation roster (who actually answers between 00:00–06:00 PST).

Thanks,
Maria
Director of Platform 
Olson Data

Attachment: requirements_rx.docx (stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maria Olson <maria.olson@olsondata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Support packaging questions

Maria — thanks, this is helpful. Short answers up front, then I'll attach a formal SKU split.

- Credits: uptime credits are calculated on calendar minutes of impacted capacity and applied monthly; we also offer an incident-level credit for lengthy P0s in the Dedicated plan (rare). We'll include a worked example.
- Response SLA: our 1-hour P0 response is first contact + assignment of an on-call engineer; target mitigation windows are separate (e.g., 4–8 hours depending on root cause and capacity).
- Discounts: we can offer a structured discount matrix for 12/24 month commitments and an optional seat-based retainer (per named on-call seat) instead of pure per-incident credits. Seat retainers convert to incident credits if unused.

On APAC coverage: our global escalation roster has overlap but we can commit to a named rotating roster for Olson if you take the 24-month retainer option.

I'll send the SKUs and two counteroffer scenarios: (A) 12-month commit with 10% discount + standard retainer and (B) 24-month commit with 18% discount + dedicated named roster and faster escalation triage.

Sharing the SKU PDF now.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Support packaging questions (internal)

Forwarding Maria's note — procurement will push hard on list price. A few internal items to align on before I send counter: 

- Pricing math: if we do seat-retainer, what's the conversion formula to credits? Propose: 1 paid seat = 3 incident credits / quarter (example).
- Escalation named roster: we should only promise a named roster for 24-month or >$X ARR deals — otherwise offer named handoff + priority paging.
- Legal ask: the customer may request a clause that credits apply automatically if pager noise exceeds X% — we should avoid open-ended clauses.

Rishi — can you run a quick TCO sim (tokens + support retainer) for Olson's projected 2.5M tokens/month on the two scenarios? Ben — prep a short note on how seat-retainer impacts on-call staffing cost.

Thanks — I want to keep this tight; Maria's procurement window is next week.

-Monica
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Quick numbers attached (spreadsheet tab: Olson_TCO). Key assumptions:
- 2.5M tokens/month baseline; 20% seasonal spike in Q4.
- Dedicated capacity cost (GPU pool) estimated at $Xk/month — modeled per existing RDW pricing.
- Seat-retainer conversion: 1 seat -> 4 incident credits / quarter (I pushed to 4 given expected SRE load). If customer prefers conservative 3 credits, we should price that ~8% higher.

Scenario A (12mo, 10% discount + standard retainer): net ARR YYYk, estimated monthly cost = $ZZZk.
Scenario B (24mo, 18% discount + named roster): net ARR ~YYYk lower with predictable on-call burden; increases Redwood staffing cost by ~12% but reduces incident churn.

Recommendation: lead with Scenario B as the preferred (better for Olson's SRE constraints), but present A as quick-commit close.

-Rishi

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: split Premium Support SKUs + explicit escalation path

Maria — thanks for the patience and the clear asks. Attached is a concise counteroffer and the escalation appendix. Highlights: 

1) SLA & credits: uptime credits are pro-rated by calendar minutes for platform-level outages; separate incident credits will be applied for P0s > 120 minutes (one-time credit at incident closure). Example table included.
2) Response: 1-hour P0 = acknowledgement + named on-call assignment. Target mitigation windows: P0 (4 hours), P1 (24 hours), P2 (3 business days). We will include a named escalation point during Olson's APAC midnight window if you select the 24-month retainer.
3) Pricing options (two scenarios):
   - Scenario A — 12mo commit: 10% off list, standard retainer (seat conversion: 1 seat = 3 credits/quarter).
   - Scenario B — 24mo commit: 18% off list, named rotating roster + priority paging (seat conversion: 1 seat = 4 credits/quarter).

4) Legal: proposed cap on credits per quarter (to prevent open-ended clause). We will not accept a pager-noise clause tied to an X% metric; we will instead include a triage SLT (Service Level Threshold) and joint-runbook governance item.

Next steps: if you want us to circulate a redline-ready SOW and DocuSign, we can have a clean version to you by EOD Friday if you confirm Scenario B. If you prefer Scenario A, we can run procurement pricing now and push to DocuSign the same timeline.

Appended: short escalation roster (names redacted until signature) and worked example credit math.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
